title: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) Lead
description:
Where dreams and reality collide and the output is, out of this world. At Redwire Space, we are a team of dreamers and doers. Where the impossible becomes possible, and every day is an opportunity to learn and get one step closer to knowing the unknown. Join us on our mission to expand humanity’s presence in space.

At Redwire, we develop and deliver advanced technologies that support our nation’s most critical missions. Our teams work alongside government customers, engineers, and program personnel to solve complex technical challenges while protecting some of the most sensitive information and systems in the Department of Defense.

We believe cybersecurity is an enabler—not a roadblock. Our Information Systems Security Officers work directly with engineering, IT, and program leadership to build secure, compliant systems that support mission needs. If you enjoy solving technical problems, collaborating with engineers, and taking ownership of classified information systems from concept through deployment, we’d like to hear from you.

Summary

Redwire Space Inc. is seeking an experienced Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO) to support multiple classified information systems across DoD, Intelligence Community, and Special Access Program (SAP) environments.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing cybersecurity compliance with hands-on technical work. The successful candidate will work closely with program managers, system security engineers, administrators, the ISSM, government officials, and facility security personnel to ensure secure operations, continuous compliance, and successful mission execution.

This position requires a self-starter who is comfortable working independently, communicating with technical and non-technical stakeholders, managing cybersecurity documentation, and driving initiatives across the full system lifecycle.

Responsibilities include:

- Manage the cybersecurity posture of classified information systems throughout the Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle.

- Responsible for the certification and accreditation of computer networks and standalone information systems using applicable government standards.

- Develop, maintain, and implement System Security Plans (SSPs) and related documentation that accurately reflect contractual and customer requirements.

- Prepare, maintain, and update POA&Ms, Security Assessment Reports, hardware/software inventories, network diagrams, and RMF artifacts.

- Support ATO, IATT, and continuous monitoring activities, ensuring systems remain compliant and mission-ready.

- Conduct ongoing vulnerability testing to verify security features and operating controls using tools such as ACAS/Nessus; coordinate remediation with engineering and administration teams.

- Perform DISA STIG compliance reviews and assist with secure configuration implementation.

- Review and coordinate engineering changes for cybersecurity impacts; support configuration management and change control activities.

- Maintain cybersecurity artifacts within eMASS or customer-specified repositories.

Oversee day-to-day security operations for all assigned information systems (classified and unclassified).

- Interact directly with internal and external customers, including government security officials, to address routine cybersecurity issues, reporting requirements, system access briefings, and inspections.

- Develop and implement facility procedures for marking, handling, transporting, sanitizing, reusing, and destroying media and equipment containing classified information.

- Coordinate changes to classified system components, environments, and physical locations, including temporary relocations.

- Assist the ISSM in reporting, documenting, and mitigating information system security incidents; initiate corrective measures to prevent recurrence.

- Support secure media handling, sanitization, COMSEC activities, and classified data management.

- Partner with engineering teams throughout system design, development, integration, testing, deployment, and sustainment to ensure security is incorporated into every phase.

- Provide cybersecurity guidance and technical expertise to cross‑functional teams.

Ideal Experience

Successful candidates will bring a blend of technical proficiency, analytical thinking, and strong communication skills. Experience in the following areas is highly desirable:

- Risk Management Framework (RMF)

- Special Access Programs (SAP) and Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) experience

- Stand‑alone classified systems

- Air‑gapped environments

- SCIF operations

- Continuous Monitoring (CONMON)

- Vulnerability Management

- Security engineering

- Network/system administration

- Engineering development environments

- Government cybersecurity inspections

- Configuration/change management

- Cross-functional technical collaboration

- COMSEC

Desired Skills

This role works closely with systems and network engineering teams. Candidates should be comfortable with:

• TCP/IP networking

• Layer 2/Layer 3 networking

• VLANs, routing, switching

• Cisco networking equipment

• Firewalls and ACLs

• Network segmentation

• Active Directory

• DNS, DHCP, Group Policy

• Network authentication

• Secure remote administration

• Packet capture and troubleshooting tools

• Secure network architecture and boundary protection

Grow with us as we innovate the next generation capabilities for a new era of space exploration! We offer a highly competitive benefits package along with a commitment to our core values of Integrity, Innovation, Impact, Inclusion, and Excellence.

Don’t meet every single requirement above? No worries. We want people who can grow, collaborate and build a stronger team. We strive to build a diverse and inclusive culture, so if you’re excited about this job posting, we encourage you to apply. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Pay Range

$110,000 - $175,000/yr.

How We Determine What We Pay (Compensation Philosophy)

Redwire determines pay for positions using local, national, and industry-specific survey data, for our locations throughout the US. We will evaluate external equity and the cost of labor/prevailing wage index, in the relative marketplace for jobs directly comparable to jobs within our company.

Salaries will be based on the applicant’s level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and internal equity within the company for the same position. An employee/candidate with a stronger skill set will receive higher pay.

title: IT Compliance Auditor (Internal Controls Auditor)
description:
Join our team of innovators and get a chance to work alongside a team of talented, curious people that are passionate about designing and deploying solutions that are accelerating humanity’s expansion into space.

Summary:

Redwire Space, Inc. has a current opportunity for a skilled and experienced IT Compliance Auditor (Analyst) to join our dynamic team at Redwire. In this capacity, you will play a crucial role in helping our organization achieve overarching governance objectives by executing our framework of IT controls that support compliance with Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) as well as other governmental regulations that we must remain in compliance with. You will also help to ensure that our IT systems, processes, and controls are effective, efficient, and compliant with applicable standards. The ideal candidate should possess a strong background in IT risk management and/or auditing, excellent project management and communication skills, and a proven ability to meet objectives and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. The IT Compliance Auditor interacts with the CIO Group, SOX Project Management Office, Internal Audit, and other stakeholders within Redwire as required.

While the position is primarily remote, the ideal candidates would live within a reasonable commutable distance to one of our Redwire Space locations, though not required. You’ll be expected to work onsite as needed for key activities.

Responsibilities:

- Lead and manage the execution of IT controls – including but not limited to management review controls, IT application controls, and key report validations – in accordance with our established control framework, management directives, and industry best practices

- Create and maintain clear, comprehensive, high-quality documentation that meets audit requirements and proves our IT controls are suitably designed and operating effectively

- Assist in management of audit projects by serving as a primary point of contact for the internal and external audit teams, coordinating walkthroughs and touchpoints, fulfilling audit evidence requests, and responding to auditor inquiries

- Perform root cause and impact analysis of identified control deficiencies or gaps, and work with stakeholders to develop, execute, and monitor control remediation plans

- Provide guidance to IT control owners across the organization on the intended design, operation, and documentation of their assigned controls

- Make approved updates to IT control frameworks, control narratives, process flows, and other related compliance documentation as needed

- Develop a foundational understanding of our business processes and IT systems in order to provide insights and recommendations to management on enhancing IT controls, mitigating risks, and improving our overall IT governance and compliance posture

- Prepare accurate and insightful reporting for senior management and executive stakeholders

- Assist the Cybersecurity team with cybersecurity incident response as required and overall protection of information assets

- Stay current with emerging trends, technologies, and regulatory changes in the IT audit landscape

Ideal Experience

- Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business administration, or related field, with a minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in IT SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, risk management, or related field, preferably in a professional services firm or corporate environment

- Experienced in conducting IT audit procedures, including risk assessment, control testing, and audit documentation, using industry-leading tools and techniques

- Experienced in managing multiple workstreams simultaneously while meeting deadlines and delivering high-quality work products in a time sensitive environment

- Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with management, team members, and stakeholders at all levels of the organization

- Must be a US Citizen due to access to controlled information systems and security vulnerability information

- Flexibility to travel to Redwire sites in North America and Europe as needed and provide remote support across time zones from US Pacific Time (UTC-8) to Eastern European Time (UTC+3)

Desired Experience

- Experience with relevant IT audit and cybersecurity standards (e.g., CMMC, NIST, NIS2, ISO 27001, NASA, DOE or DHS Cybersecurity requirements)

- Master's degree or professional certifications (CISA, CISSP, CIA, etc.) are preferred but not required

- Experience in the aerospace or defense industry

- Experience working with US federal government contractors and associated requirements

- Experience working as an incident responder on an operational network

In this role, you will support the development of a new spacecraft designed for very‑low Earth orbit (VLEO) missions. You will work closely with lead systems engineers on requirements management, interface management, customer deliverables, and cross-functional coordination. The ideal candidate has a strong systems-thinking mindset, thrives in a fast-paced environment, and is comfortable supporting complex technical decision-making across multidisciplinary engineering teams.

Responsibilities

- Support lead systems engineers in managing system and subsystem requirements, including requirements decomposition, flow-down, verification method identification, and customer coordination.

- Drive interface management activities, ensuring clear definition, communication, and maintenance of mechanical, electrical, and data interfaces across engineering teams.

- Contribute to customer deliverables such as requirements documents, interface control documents, verification plans, and milestone review artifacts.

- Collaborate across engineering functional groups to evaluate design decisions, support down‑selection of COTS components, and ensure physical implementations meet functional and performance requirements.

- Support development of a new spacecraft bus and payload accommodations optimized for VLEO environments, including consideration of environmental constraints, system-level performance drivers, and operational needs.

- Participate in cross-functional engineering trades, risk assessments, and technical reviews to ensure coherent system architecture and traceability.

- Assist in planning and tracking verification and validation activities aligned to system requirements and program milestones.

- Contribute to integration and test readiness by supporting the creation of test plans, reviewing test setups, and ensuring alignment with verification objectives.

- Communicate effectively with program leadership, engineering teams, and customers to convey technical status, risks, and mitigation strategies.

Required Qualifications

- Bachelor of Science in a STEM discipline with 2–4 years of experience, or a Master’s with 0–2 years of experience.

- Proven experience within an engineering discipline, including requirements development, subsystem design, and integration & test.

- Demonstrated initiative and ability to solve complex problems.

- Self‑motivated in applying engineering principles, concepts, and practices of mechanical/aerospace engineering to independently perform assignments.

- Familiarity with NASA or DoD lifecycle reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR).

- U.S. Citizenship required, with ability to obtain a DoD Security Clearance.

Desired Qualifications

- M.S. degree in Systems Engineering.

- Experience working on spacecraft systems and subsystems.

- Experience developing, managing, and decomposing requirements and identifying verification methods/approaches.

- Experience developing test plans and managing hardware test campaigns.

- Experience with requirements management tools such as JAMA or DOORS.

- Experience with interface management and control within complex systems.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

- Experience with Microsoft Project and Visio.

- Active DoD Security Clearance preferred.

- Experience with Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE).
